To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TDF is associated with renal dysfunction in HIV-infected patients.
the estimated glomerular function rate (eGFr) of HIV-infected Koreans decreased significantly after 48 weeks of tenofovir disoproxl fumarate (tenofovir) treatment.
Tenofovir use is associated with decreased kidney function in HIV-infested Korean people.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changes in renal function among HIV-infected Koreans during the first year of TDF use.
the long-term changes in renal function among HIV-infected Koreans who are receiving TDF.
the long-term patterns and predictors of change in renal function among HIV-infected Koreans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

renal function should be monitored at 3-month intervals during the first year of ART with TDF, and at least annually thereafter, and that TDF should not be prescribed to patients with eGFR (creatinine) <60 mL/min/1,73 m2.
the long-term use of tenofovir disoproxi fumarate (tenofovir DF) may be associated with renal dysfunction.
TDF is a well-tolerated drug, but that renal function should be monitored in all patients receiving this drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TDF is a safe drug for the treatment of HIV infection in Korean patients.

the renal function of patients receiving TDF was decreased over time and that the decrease in renal function was more pronounced in patients receiving TDF-based first-line ART than in ART-naïve patients.

the renal function of patients receiving first-line ART including TDF is significantly decreased compared to those receiving ART-naïve, and the renal function of those receiving first-line ART was decreased during the follow up period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to closely monitor renal function in HIV patients receiving long-term Tenofovir.
the use of tenofovir should be carefully monitored, especially in patients with pre-existing renal dysfunction or in those who have been on tenofovir for a long period of time.
the use of TDF in HIV-infected patients is associated with renal injury.
